lens: Buildability in Figma Motion (beta), judged by an engineer who knows the toolbox. I checked four things: whether every move can be written with the listed fields, whether the pivot, size and counter-translation maths holds, how many layers, tracks and keys each spec needs, and what will not render as described. I checked the type spec's keyframes by parsing spec-type.keyframes.json. For the other two I counted keys from their tables and recomputed the geometry by hand. I also measured one fact that all three depend on. In the current ad's MP4, the Scene 2 photo edge at frames 89–96 sits at 927, 669, 477, 339, 242, 173, 124 and 89 px. That matches cubic:0.16,1,0.3,1 evaluated at t = k/30 to the pixel; centre-of-frame sampling would give 789, 565 and so on. So Figma samples frame k at exactly k/30, and its cubic curve is the same as CSS cubic-bezier. That makes every computed peak speed, blur placement and frame-exact cut in these specs trustworthy. One limit also comes from the tool's schema (src/server/tools/motion.ts): a track holds at most 100 keyframes, and each call replaces the whole track, so a longer track cannot be split across calls.

scores.spec: spec-type.md — Moku: "Slow down." (type-led IG Story ad)
scores.reasons:
EXPRESSIBLE AND MACHINE-CHECKED. It is the only spec whose keys exist as data. Parsed from the JSON: 92 animated layers, 158 tracks, 611 keys, at most 7 keys per track and 6 tracks per layer, no repeated times, last key 14.4. The only off-grid keys are the 36 deliberate cut pairs, and the 22 LAYER_BLUR prerequisites match the effect tracks exactly. In total it needs about 166 layers: 92 figma_set_keyframes calls and 22 figma_set_effects calls. The cut pairs at k/30 − 0.025 / k/30 − 0.005 (for example S1 · Hook OPACITY 2.375 / 2.395) are proven safe by the sampling measurement.

PIVOT AND COUNTER-TRANSLATION MATHS IS CORRECT EVERYWHERE I CHECKED:
- S1/Window WIDTH 96→480 with TRANSLATION_X 192→0, and S1/Photo −192, keeps the slit centred on x 540.
- S2/Iris W/H 2→3000 with TRANSLATION_XY 1499→0, and S2/Plate −1499, is exactly screen-locked. The iris reaches every corner: the farthest is 1419 px against 1480.
- The S3/Window shutter (HEIGHT 1040→8, TRANSLATION_Y 516, S3/Inner −516) stays centred on y 1060, and FX/Edge ±520 lands on y 540 and 1580.
- The S6/CTA field morph (1080×1920 → 520×112, TRANSLATION_XY −280,−1160 → 0,0) keeps x 540 throughout. Its 13.2 pulse fires when WIDTH is back at rest, so the pivot is unambiguous.
- The Top bar fill:0 flip at frame 68 is the right frame: the iris radius is 491 px at f67 and 621 at f68, against 575 px to the farthest glyph. Still, for 1–2 frames part of "Moku" and the label is ink-on-ink, which whole-node colour flips cannot avoid.

RISKS:
- It is the heaviest build.
- Every mask "hugs", which means it is an auto-layout frame, so about 40 animated letters and words are auto-layout children whose TRANSLATION is unmeasured.
- STACK_SPACING is unmeasured and drives frame 0 (S1/Slow 56→−8 over 0–0.6), S5/Ten and S6/Logo.
- A 3000 px iris whose round shape relies on corner-radius clamping, with blur, sits inside a container that carries a 28 px whip blur.

WILL NOT RENDER AS DESCRIBED:
- Round-cap trims at zero length have no opacity guard, so stray cap dots are possible: S2/Orbit 1.8–3.0, the S3 ticks at start = end = 0.5, S5/Divider 8.4–9.6, S6/Rule 11.0–11.7.
- S3/Dim line sits in S3/Inner, not in the pushing S3/Shot, so it ends up about 8–13 px off the vase's top and bottom.
- The FX edge bars "meet as one line" but leave a 2 px sliver of the slit between them (y 1059–1061).

OVERALL RISK: medium. Each of the three big risks has a named fallback.
scores.keep:
The frame-0 hook, built cheaply:
- "S l o w" tracking collapses (one STACK_SPACING track) while the image slit opens (WIDTH plus a counter TRANSLATION_X).
- "down." drops per letter with 2-frame staggers and blur on the fastest frames.

The type literally slows down, it is already moving on frame 0, and the whole hook is about 12 tracks. Also keep this spec's build method for whatever ships: keyframes generated as JSON from one source, plus the cut-pair convention.
scores.fatal: None. Closest: frame 0 depends on two unmeasured mechanisms, STACK_SPACING reflow and TRANSLATION on auto-layout children. Probe both before building S2. The fallback is a TRANSLATION_X track on each letter.

scores.spec: spec-graphic.md — One circle of clay (Moku IG Story, graphic shape-led cut)
scores.reasons:
EXPRESSIBLE, AND THE GEOMETRY CLOSES:
- The Disc goes SCALE 1.05→0.1116 (Ø 96) with TRANSLATION_X −210 and TRANSLATION_Y −150 over 2.1–2.4, landing on (330, 1020). That is exactly where the Band window's Ø 96 dot sits (TRANSLATION_X 282, TRANSLATION_Y 612), and Push's −282 / −612 counter keeps the vase still.
- The S2 switch-on at 2.3 happens under the disc: the dot is 206 px from the disc centre, against a 370 px radius.
- The Iris W/H 2↔780↔812, with TRANSLATION_X/Y 389 and −16, stays centred on (540, 1170).
- The Kiln window counters put the bowl at screen (15, 785) and the plates at (79, 315). Both cover their windows.
- The Terracotta field rule (TRANSLATION_X = 320 − W/2, TRANSLATION_Y = −20 − H/2) holds (540, 1080) on the IRIS curve, and the collapse lands on y 1100–1220 with x held at 540.
- The Brand bug scaled 3.5× about its own centre goes from (152, 300) to (540, 660), which matches the 616×252 logo.
- It is the only spec with opacity guards on every round-cap trim and every seed shape.
- Every HOLD fires under cover. The 3-decimal times put the x.x67 HOLDs one frame LATER than written (Disc OPACITY 2.467 fires on frame 75, not 74), but they are still covered by the bursting band, so it is harmless.

COUNT: about 127 layers, about 85 animated, about 155 tracks, about 606 keys (plus 144 for the grain), and 13 blur prerequisites, which match the tracks.

RISKS AND WHAT WILL NOT RENDER AS DESCRIBED:
- The grain boil is 144 TRANSLATION_XY keys on one track, over the 100-key cap, so the call is refused as written. Re-grid it to every 0.15 s (97 keys).
- The bug-as-logo is a LAYER_BLUR'd frame scaled 3.5×. It may be rasterised at its original size and then enlarged, leaving a soft "Moku" for the whole 2.9 s end card.
- The kicker's STACK_SPACING on a HUG row, with a compensating TRANSLATION_X, relies on the hug width reflowing during playback, which is unmeasured.
- The Cream circle and the terracotta bloom (Ø 2420 centred on 540, 1080) clear the top corners (1207.5 px away) by only 2.5 px.
- Five size morphs that rely on the R 9999 radius being clamped are each a counter-translation pair. All of them, about 606 keys, must be hand-transcribed from the @-notation, with no generated JSON; one slip breaks a match cut.

OVERALL RISK: medium on mechanism, high on precision and effort.
scores.keep: The clay disc collapsing (SCALE plus TRANSLATION, ease-in, 2.1–2.4) into a Ø 96 dot exactly on the vase belly, which then bursts into the image band. The band is a clip frame morphing from circle to rectangle (W/H, TRANSLATION_X/Y, CORNER_RADIUS) with a counter-translated Push, over 2.4–2.9. It is a true shape match cut, and its maths is airtight. Also keep its discipline of swapping images only under full cover with HOLD.
scores.fatal: None. Closest: the bug→logo enlargement may render soft for the whole end card. Build the fallback Logo swap at 11.533 by default instead of as a contingency.

scores.reasons:
LOWEST MECHANISM RISK AND SMALLEST BUILD. The masks are plain frames with no auto-layout, so no animated text is an auto-layout child. There is only one STACK_SPACING track (S1 Row Moku), with exact per-letter TRANSLATION_X fallback numbers, and LEFT/TOP constraints are stated for every child of a size-animated frame.

THE MATHS CHECKS:
- S1 and S2 form a film strip exactly 1920 px apart (0 / 30 / −1920 against 1920 / 1950 / 0).
- The SCALE_Y 1.1 smear about each container's own centre makes a 192 px OVERLAP at 2.4, with S2 over S1, not a gap, so it is safe.
- The S2 Circle shrinks to 840 × 0.94 = 790, the same size as the S3 Window circle at (145, 298), on the same centre (540, 693).
- In the T3 dive, TRANSLATION_Y = (693 − 960)(1 − 2.6) = 427 holds the anchor point.
- With an 880 px pitch, each strip window lands at x 120.

COUNT: about 117 layers, 72 animated (with the grain), about 127 tracks, about 472 keys (plus 145 for the grain), and about 18 blur prerequisites.

WILL NOT RENDER AS DESCRIBED:
1. FX Grain has 145 HOLD keys, over the 100-key cap, so it is refused.
2. S5 Arch at HEIGHT 1 is the TOP layer of S5's three, so from 10.8 to 11.233 a 540 × 1 px line of photo at y 907 lies over the bowl and then on top of both irises. It needs an OPACITY guard.
3. The S5 CTA Pill pops SCALE 0.01→1 (11.867–12.0) while its WIDTH is 116, not its rest of 600, with TRANSLATION_X 242. Whether the pivot is the centre of the animated box or of the resting box is unmeasured. If it is the resting box, the dot appears near x 782 and slides to 540.
4. T4 Iris A/B have no blur track. The computed radius jumps from 421 to 842 px between frames 331 and 332, exactly the strobing edge the critique condemned.
5. The S3 Dim SVG paths carry no stroke attributes (the prose says stroke 2), so imported as written they render nothing.
6. S3 Photo SCALE 1→1.05 pivots on the photo's centre (794, 579), so the belly drifts about 4 px by 5.4 and about 13 px by 7.8. That fails the spec's own ±2 px check (cosmetic).

The keys are hand-transcribed from tables. OVERALL RISK: low to medium, and every defect is a one-track fix.
scores.keep: The T3 push-through. S3 Hero goes SCALE 1→2.6 with an anchor-compensating TRANSLATION_Y on the same ease-in curve, plus blur 0→18. At 7.8 it cuts, matched in speed, into S4 Content 0.82→1 on expo-out with blur 18→0. That is four tracks on two containers with no masks: the cheapest high-impact transition in any of the three specs. The T1 film-strip whip (two containers keyed 1920 px apart) is a close second.
scores.fatal: None. Closest: the end-card handoff has two finish defects on top of each other, the unblurred iris edges and the 1 px Arch line drawn over them, and the CTA dot's pivot is unverified while its WIDTH is animated. Each is a one-track fix.

recommendation:
Ranked on build risk alone:
1. **Camera spec:** the smallest build, with the fewest unmeasured mechanisms and plain-frame masks. Its defects are small and each is a one-track fix.
2. **Type spec:** the heaviest build, but the only one specified as machine-checked data, and its frame-exact cuts are proven safe.
3. **Graphic spec:** the most tightly interlocked. Five counter-translated morphs plus a bug-to-logo enlargement, all hand-transcribed.

None of the three has a fatal flaw. Whichever spec wins on craft, build it this way:

**(1) Build method.**
- Generate one keyframes JSON from a single source, as the type spec does.
- Put every key on the 1/30 s grid.
- Keep cuts as LINEAR pairs at k/30 − 0.025 and k/30 − 0.005. This is now measured to be exactly safe: Figma samples frame k at t = k/30, and its cubic curve is the same as CSS cubic-bezier.

**(2) Masks.** Prefer the camera spec's plain clip frames, with no auto-layout, for every animated word or letter. Keep auto-layout only for rows whose STACK_SPACING animates.

**(3) Probe before scene 2.** Spend one short probe render, about 2 s, on the five mechanisms all three specs rely on but nobody has measured:
- STACK_SPACING reflow, including on a HUG row.
- Corner-radius clamping while WIDTH or HEIGHT animates.
- TRANSLATION on an auto-layout child.
- The SCALE pivot while WIDTH differs from its rest value.
- Whether a round-capped trim at zero length leaves a dot.

**(4) Global fixes.**
- Keep any repeated-key track at 100 keys or fewer. Run the grain every 0.15 s, or leave it static as the type spec does.
- Put an OPACITY guard on every collapsed mask and every round-cap trim.
- Ramp blur on every edge moving faster than about 150 px per frame (the camera spec's irises lack it).
- Make bloom circles at least 2480 px.
- Scale a node only while its WIDTH is at rest.
- Build the graphic spec's real-logo fallback by default.

**(5) Elements to carry into the final ad, whichever spec wins:**
- the type spec's "S l o w" tracking-collapse hook;
- the graphic spec's disc-to-vase-belly match cut;
- the camera spec's push-through;
- the terracotta field collapsing into the CTA pill, which the type and graphic specs both have. It is five tracks on one rectangle.

Note for the main agent: the frame-sampling measurement (current ad, frames 89–96) could become a claims-registry entry. I did not edit the registry.
